headline: High: shared file-based workflows can leak data and create write conflicts; prompt-injection risk is low because pathway has no input surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, MCP, or browser surfaces, so direct injection into pathway is blocked. agent_b can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so only an unusual manual copy-paste or external file bridge could carry attacker text into pathway. The pairwise pathway is weak and not default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_b output into a file or prompt consumed by agent_a
IF a shared external file is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable manual copy-paste between outputs and prompts
Use a provenance tag on any transferred text
Review any shared files before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while agent_b touches text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data and can read files plus use broad network egress. If both are pointed at the same workspace, agent_b can ingest and transmit content that pathway processes, creating a realistic leakage path in default configurations.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same directory or dataset
IF agent_b is allowed to send retrieved file contents to external services
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict agent_b network egress
Mount shared data read-only
Redact sensitive files before processing
Log all outbound requests from agent_b

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a cannot write files or modify git state, but agent_b can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances. That reduces direct contention, yet shared mutable resources still create conflict if both are attached to the same directory or repo. Uncertainty is limited because agent_a's write surface is absent, but the shared-workspace pathway remains plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable directory
IF agent_b is used to edit files that pathway also reads or generates
mitigations: Give each agent its own directory
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Disable concurrent writes to the same repo
Stage changes through a single coordinator

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a document-processing system with no explicit verification or action-taking controls, and agent_b exposes pipeline-style tool use plus stdin/stdout and file access. If agent_b consumes pathway output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from agent_a can propagate into downstream documents or scripts. The pairwise risk exists even without direct evidence of a specific workflow.
conditions: IF agent_b treats pathway output as ground truth without validation
IF pathway output is fed into scripts or generated artifacts
mitigations: Add a human review step
Require schema validation on pathway output
Cross-check outputs against source documents
Mark pathway output as untrusted metadata

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. However, agent_b can process multimodal data and use broad egress, so compliance gaps could arise if regulated data is routed through it. agent_a is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through agent_b
IF retention or logging policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Document retention settings
Disable unnecessary logging
Confirm data-processing region before deployment
